# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Economic Vision

The Conservatives present their manifesto as a continuation of economic recovery following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis. They highlight falling inflation (from 11.1% to 2.3%), rising real wages, and returning growth as evidence their plan is working. The party commits to reducing borrowing and debt while maintaining fiscal rules.

## Key Tax Pledges

The centrepiece is cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, saving average workers £1,350 annually. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The new "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees both State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowances rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household system, with families keeping benefits until combined income reaches £120,000.

## Immigration and Borders

The party pledges to introduce a legally binding cap on migration, with numbers falling annually. They commit to continuing Rwanda deportation flights and stopping illegal Channel crossings. Legal migration thresholds have already been raised, with the Skilled Worker visa salary requirement increased to £38,700.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, representing the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The manifesto emphasises continued support for Ukraine and maintaining the nuclear deterrent. A new National Defence and Resilience Plan would be developed.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The party promises 8,000 additional neighbourhood police officers and continued investment in schools, maintaining real-terms per-pupil funding.

## Housing and Infrastructure

The target is 1.6 million new homes, with permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. £36 billion from cancelled HS2 savings would fund local transport improvements, including £8.3 billion for road repairs.

## Young People

A mandatory National Service programme would offer 18-year-olds either military placements or community volunteering. The party commits to 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing poor-quality university courses, plus mobile phone bans in schools.

## Energy and Environment

The approach balances net zero commitments with pragmatism, guaranteeing no new green levies while accelerating renewables. Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds would continue. Nuclear power expansion includes Small Modular Reactors approval within 100 days.
